question: to the Commission Tamás Deutsch (PfE), Kinga Gál (PfE), Enikő Győri (PfE), András Gyürk (PfE), Viktória Ferenc (PfE), György Hölvényi (PfE), Csaba Dömötör (PfE), András László (PfE), Ernő Schaller-Baross (PfE), Pál Szekeres (PfE) Subject:

Article 11 of the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union guarantees everyone the right to freedom of expression, including the freedom to receive and impart information and ideas without interference by public authority. Furthermore, EU media legislation requires public service media to operate independently and impartially, with their management selected through transparent, objective and non-discriminatory procedures. The European Media Freedom Act also aims to protect media freedom and editorial independence from political and economic interference. Following the Hungarian Government’s decision to suspend the news services of Hungary’s public service television, radio and online news portal: 1.

Does the Commission consider that this decision is compatible with Article 11 of the Charter of Fundamental Rights, which guarantees the right to receive and impart information without interference by public authority?

Does the Commission consider that the suspension of public service media news services and the Government’s intervention in their operation are compatible with the EU rules safeguarding the independence and impartiality of public service media, including the European Media Freedom Act?
answer: (English version) to the Commission Tamás Deutsch (PfE), Kinga Gál (PfE), Enikő Győri (PfE), András Gyürk (PfE), Viktória Ferenc (PfE), György Hölvényi (PfE), Csaba Dömötör (PfE), András László (PfE), Ernő Schaller-Baross (PfE), Pál Szekeres (PfE) (28 July 2026) Subject: Compatibility of the suspension of Hungarian public service media news services with EU law Article 11 of the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union guarantees everyone the right to freedom of expression, including the freedom to receive and impart information and ideas without interference by public authority. Furthermore, EU media legislation requires public service media to operate independently and impartially, with their management selected through transparent, objective and non-discriminatory procedures. The European Media Freedom Act also aims to protect media freedom and editorial independence from political and economic interference. Following the Hungarian Government’s decision to suspend the news services of Hungary’s public service television, radio and online news portal: 1.

Does the Commission consider that this decision is compatible with Article 11 of the Charter of Fundamental Rights, which guarantees the right to receive and impart information without interference by public authority?

Does the Commission consider that the suspension of public service media news services and the Government’s intervention in their operation are compatible with the EU rules safeguarding the independence and impartiality of public service media, including the European Media Freedom Act?

(21 September 2026) The Commission notes that amendments to the Hungarian Media Act, adopted in June 2026, brought about the termination of the previous Public Service Foundation and the establishment of a new Independent Public Media Board. The legislation establishes new rules regulating the composition of the new Board, nominations thereto, the termination of office and its respective tasks, powers and remuneration of office holders thereof as well as rules governing the public service media provider itself, including the appointment of the provider’s Chief Executive Officer, its financing and management. A key requirement of the European Media Freedom Act (EMFA) (1) is that Member States shall ensure that public service media providers are editorially and functionally independent and provide in an impartial manner a plurality of information and opinions to their audiences. The Commission understands that the suspension of broadcasts was a temporary step in the context of the above-mentioned reform, with the above-mentioned goals in mind and that the service has resumed. The Commission will continue exchanges with the Hungarian authorities in the context of the enforcement of the EMFA.

Regulation (EU) 2024/1083 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 April 2024 establishing a common framework for media services in the internal market and amending Directive 2010/13/EU (European Media Freedom Act).
